claim: The command guard change K4 (scripts/hooks/secret_path_guard.py, sha256 33a11fc01ee35dc4b157b04eee4a8524460bb3fe74375ee32485bc3b2530782f, 275,624 bytes) adds runner-command reading, bounded interpreter reading and OmniRoute management-route, manager-environment, store, ps and canary rules on top of the K3 guard (sha256 a70a056fc27524c65ea5ce4db43fe712cabb44cf9b171866abf805d7306d3b51, merged in PR #511 as 5597f9fa). On 2026-10-01 the coordinator replayed 1,524 documented repository commands through K4 against K3 and against the installed guard (sha256 f9be81b240762dc58da874f135040d182ca9fb5e9056ab9b8a977dd909453244): 0 newly blocked, 0 loosened and 0 reason changed against each. The acceptance oracle found 0 adjusted and 0 reason mismatches over 338 cases, and a scan of 16,315 distinct lines and blocks from 9,329 tracked files found 0 newly blocked and 0 loosened against K3. The repair worker's mutation gate killed 461 of 461 mutants by failures of named permanent tests. A read-only GPT-6 re-check of the one repair round (guard sha256 d4d4bef2…, before two later one-line fixes from PR review threads) found every finding of the GPT-6 verification and the Opus review fixed, apart from stale metadata in an untracked handoff, and no input that K3 refuses and K4 allows outside the contract's form F across 8,602 differential inputs. Through a real hook process the verification's two timeout generators answered in 0.20 and 0.22 s. The re-check found five further items, recorded as residuals.
limitations: Local integration on one host plus read-only cross-family reviews, not a proof: the checks compare text heuristics on finite corpora (the repository's tables, fenced commands, tracked files, generated mutations and the reviewers' differential inputs), and a review that finds nothing does not show that nothing exists.

Evidence classes differ: the replay, the oracle, the corpus scan, the gitleaks ancestry scan and the targeted suites were run by the coordinator on the final head; the mutation gate and the differential counts come from the repair worker's and the re-check's recorded output, not from a coordinator rerun.

The targeted suites' one failure is by design: test_host_profile_copy_is_verbatim compares the installed host copy with the repository file, and the host copy stays the installed guard until K3 and K4 are merged and reinstalled after the Gate A window closes.

test_k4_timing judges each helper's growth from 25k to 100k characters by the criterion of #556 (an exponent ln((t100k + 5 ms) / (t25k + 5 ms)) / ln 4 under 1.5 over the elementwise minimum of up to three rounds), which replaced a single-sample 8x ratio after the ratio failed PR #567's hosted validate on two linear helpers at 1 to 6 % margins; with the minimum of three rounds all 67 helpers measured exponents of 0.975 or less on the workstation. Its processor-time bound is the contract's 0.5 s on the workstation and scales elsewhere by the host's time for a guard-independent shlex workload (short words and one 120,000-character quoted word) relative to the workstation's 0.188 s (never below 1), after hosted macOS runs measured linear rows at 0.522 to 0.562 s against 0.197 s here (a long quoted word lexes about 2.6 times slower there). Below about 4.4 ms at 25k a quadratic helper passes the exponent, and the host-scaled bound guards it there.

Residuals carried to the next guard change: two gateway forms that K3 and K4 both allow, a Request passed to urlopen by keyword after its body (urlopen(data=b"x", url=r)) and an augmented member assignment (r.full_url += "/x"); two false refusals K4 introduced, an incomplete computed argv item (subprocess.run(["printenv" + "-safe"]) refuses environment_dump) and a command -v lookup read as an assignment before a keyring store (keyring_store_literal); and a generated 193,560-character urllib command whose urlopen calls reuse one Request, which the re-check measured at about 1.9 s through the real hook, below the 10 s hook timeout and above the 1 s target.

The repair worker's mutation gate ran on the test file before four later test-only commits (runner-test values drawn from letters outside the hex alphabet, the growth criterion, the host-scaled bound and its long-word reference); the two mutants killed in test_k4_timing (BUDGET-DUPLICATE, CODE-CONTEXT) were killed by row verdicts and the processor-time bound, which these changes keep, and the gate was not rerun.

Two review threads on PR #567 (the Codex review bot) found two false refusals after the GPT-6 re-check: `curl -0` (HTTP/1.0) missing from the short-flag table, and `pypy3` missing from form F's interpreter expression although the contract's form-F grammar includes it. Both were fixed (guard sha256 33a11fc0…, from d4d4bef2…); the coordinator re-ran the replay, oracle, tracked-file scan, growth exponents and targeted suites on the fixed guard, but the GPT-6 re-check and the worker's mutation gate were not rerun on it.

Commit identity: the re-check reviewed commit 58dde8ef. Its history was then rewritten so a helper-name tuple no longer reads as a gitleaks generic-api-key match (one test line reordered in four commits), rebased onto main after K3 merged (5597f9fa), and extended by four test-only commits (runner test values drawn from letters outside the hex alphabet, fixing a chance-match flake; the timing criterion and host-scaled bound above); the guard bytes stayed d4d4bef2… through those steps and changed only with the two review-thread fixes.
evidence_class: local integration (documented-command replay, acceptance oracle, tracked-file scan, gitleaks ancestry scan and the targeted unit suites on this host, run by the coordinator), the repair worker's recorded mutation gate, and read-only cross-family reviews: a GPT-6 (gpt-6-astra, effort max) verification and re-check and an Opus review
